title: SSE handshake fuzz + chunk-splitting repro notes
content:
Goal: quick reproducible test for intermittent client-observed stalls/partial events when model streaming uses SSE (text/event-stream).

Summary of observed behavior:
- Clients sometimes receive fragmented JSON tokens across SSE event boundaries (e.g. a single JSON object split into two 'data:' chunks) and then either (a) client JSON parse fails, or (b) client waits until timeout for remainder.
- Happens more often when traffic is bursty or through our internal HTTP/1.1 proxy pool (envoy/nginx).
- Not consistent in staging vs local dev; seems correlated with TCP coalescing and proxy buffer heuristics.

What I'm trying to capture here: minimal CLI/straightforward repros that exercise the handshake/transfer edge cases, capture raw bytes, and test how different clients behave when chunks are split at various offsets.

Quick notes on SSE basics (reminder):
- SSE is text/event-stream, lines separated by LF (\n), events separated by blank line (\n\n).
- Each 'data:' line is appended; clients only emit when blank line seen.
- If server sends partial 'data:' (no trailing newline), some clients will buffer until newline. If newline arrives later in a separate TCP packet/chunk, behavior depends on client stream parser.

Repro experiments and commands tried (ordered by increasing fidelity):

1) Basic curl raw stream (baseline)
- Command:
  curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    "https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-mini"
- Notes: '-N' disables buffering in curl so you can observe data as it arrives. Use -v to see headers.
- Observed: sometimes curl prints partial lines followed by immediate newline when next chunk arrives; hard to see byte boundaries.

2) Inspect raw bytes with openssl s_client (TLS) -> hex dump
- Command (local warmup):
  printf 'GET /v1/stream?model=redwood-mini HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: staging.api.redwood.ai\r\nAccept: text/event-stream\r\nAuthorization: Bearer $TOKEN\r\nConnection: keep-alive\r\n\r\n' | openssl s_client -connect staging.api.redwood.ai:443 -quiet | hexdump -C
- Notes: gives exact byte boundaries. Useful to confirm if server sends CRLF vs LF only, and where chunked transfer boundaries occur.
- Observed: server uses chunked transfer encoding (no content-length). Chunk sizes match internal write() calls from runtime (likely flush policy).

3) Force artificial splitting with socat (local proxy that splits by byte count)
- Idea: create a TCP proxy that forwards but fragments writes into N-byte segments to simulate network-level splitting.
- Command:
  socat -v TCP4-LISTEN:18080,reuseaddr,fork SYSTEM:'openssl s_client -quiet -connect staging.api.redwood.ai:443'
  (then run curl against localhost:18080 with same headers)
- Variant: use 'pv -qL 50' to throttle throughput and see reassembly timing.
- Observed: when we force 1-2 byte splits inside a JSON token, some client-level SSE parsers (browser EventSource polyfills) end up dropping the event or combining oddly.

4) Node.js minimal reader to show chunks as they arrive (useful for reproducing streaming client bug)
- Script (save as quick-stream-debug.js):
  const fetch = require('node-fetch');
  (async () => {
    const res = await fetch('https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-mini', {
      headers: { 'Accept': 'text/event-stream', 'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + process.env.TOKEN }
    });
    const reader = res.body.getReader();
    let seq = 0;
    while (true) {
      const { done, value } = await reader.read();
      if (done) break;
      console.log('CHUNK', seq++, value ? value.length : 0, Buffer.from(value || []).toString());
    }
  })();
- Observed: Node fetch yields a mix of chunk sizes; sometimes we see 'data: {"delta":"Hel' then next chunk '"lo","idx":...'

5) Go minimal client to print raw frames (net/http read loop)
- Use net.Dial + fmt.Fprintln to send raw request and then read by small buffer to inspect where CRLFs exist.
- Command (one-file go program) used to assert chunk boundaries.

Representative bad trace (raw-ish, redacted):
- Raw bytes (hexdump-like):
  00000000  34 0d 0a 0d 0a 64 61 74 61 3a 20 7b 22 64 65 6c  |4....data: {"del|
  00000010  74 61 22 3a 22 48 65 6c  |ta":"Hel|
  00000019  6c 6f 22 2c 22 69 6e 64  65 78 22 3a 31 7d 0d 0a  |lo","index":1}.|

- Interpretation: chunk boundary happened inside the JSON string 'Hello' (\"Hel followed by lo\"). Client-side parser received 'data: {"delta":"Hel' then a second TCP packet with 'lo","index":1}\r\n'

Hypotheses:
- Our runtime's flush policy writes small writes as tokens are generated. Proxies (envoy/nginx) may re-chunk (coalesce) or preserve boundaries unpredictably; awaiting newline is required by SSE but mid-token splits are legal — it's on client to reassemble. However, some polyfills/old clients treat each 'data:' line as a standalone event and expect complete JSON on each line.
- When backpressure occurs, the runtime may emit zero-length heartbeats or partial 'data:' lines (maybe due to KV cache flush) that confuse clients expecting full events per write.
- HTTP/2 transliteration (if any) could be converting to DATA frames with different size semantics and resulting event delays.

Quick checklist for reproducing locally and capturing evidence:
- Reproduce with bare TLS socket to capture exact bytes (openssl s_client + hexdump).
- Run a middle proxy (socat) to induce fragmentation at byte-level.
- Try with and without charset and with Connection: keep-alive vs close (some proxies buffer until close).
- Test direct to runtime (bypass envoy) in staging to see if problem persists — helps isolate between runtime vs proxy.
- Capture tcpdump + ngrep -q -W byline 'ngrep -d any -W byline -t -q "GET /v1/stream"' on host to get raw.

Small reproduction snippet (curl + dd splitting):
- Ugly but useful: use netcat to accept server response and rewrite into chunks:
  mkfifo f; nc -l 127.0.0.1 18081 < f &
  curl -s -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    "https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-mini" > f
  # separately, use a small script to read from socket and print one byte at a time to stdout to simulate lossy client

Notes on client behavior we observed in the field:
- Browser EventSource: usually tolerant (buffers until blank line). Some older mobile polyfills deliver early 'message' events on each 'data:' line, causing JSON parse errors.
- Python requests with iter_lines(decode_unicode=True): can drop lines if keep-alive chunks are unusual; iter_lines has a 'chunk_size' param which affects behavior.
- Go bufio.NewReader.ReadString('\n') is fine as long as server sends LF. If server uses CRLF vs LF inconsistently, ReadString can still work but splitting yields partial strings.

Action plan / next steps:
- [ ] Create a small controlled server that emits 'data:' lines where we can programmatically split at arbitrary offsets. Use this to run clients in CI to verify resilience. (prototype: tiny python aiohttp SSE server with configurable chunk boundaries)
- [ ] Reproduce behind envoy with same configuration as staging; log envoy cluster buffers and upstream flush intervals.
- [ ] Add runtime option to ensure each SSE event is sent as a single write() where possible (atomic write for event) — at least as an experiment to see impact on frequency of repro.
- [ ] Add unit/integration tests that simulate 1-byte TCP fragmentation and assert client parsers still reconstruct events.
- [ ] If proxy is root cause, propose envoy config change (stream_idle_timeout/flush intervals or disable http buffer filter) and test.

Notes to SRE/Infra:
- If asking SRE for capture, request tcpdump with 1MB rotation and specify exact request id and approximate timestamp. Example capture command: sudo tcpdump -i any host staging.api.redwood.ai and port 443 -w /tmp/streaming-<ts>.pcap
- For ngrep: sudo ngrep -d any -W byline port 443 'text/event-stream' -J /tmp/stream-raw.json (might require TLS termination to see plaintext).

Logs and artifacts to attach when filing bug: hexdump outputs, node/py/go client traces (showing chunk lengths and exact strings), socat proxy logs, envoy config snippet, pcap if available.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are there any middleboxes in cloud provider path doing HTTP/1.1 -> HTTP/2 conversion that would alter framing semantics?
- Does our runtime ever send partial \"data:\" lines intentionally (e.g., flush after token generation without newline) as an optimization? If so, can we add a newline-only flush policy?

If anyone is debugging this in parallel: ping me (Priya) and drop artifacts into this doc or add to AIINF-4321. I will push a tiny python SSE server prototype and a minimal go client tomorrow for consistent CI reproduction.

Useful references and prior runs:
- local hexdump: /tmp/hexdump-sse-2026-02-20.txt (on my laptop)
- quick node reader: scripts/quick-stream-debug.js (branch: priya/sse-fuzz)
